Both systems are running Arch with the same kernel and KWin 6.5.0 on Wayland. I made a [diff of the packages](https://gist.github.com/freenull/0aa8a97c6c99f66585d4bd1f94ddc4fe) (`diff igpu_laptop_pkgs.txt dgpu_laptop_pkgs.txt`), but I haven't been able to figure anything out. I'm starting to worry the root cause might be in the GPU drivers :/\

Edit:
I did more digging.
First off: this affects only the NVIDIA Vulkan userspace driver (580.95.05). It works fine with AMD drivers. It is reproducible in the Vulkan driver specifically and does not affect the OpenGL driver.
I built a version of Godot with debug symbols and attached to it with GDB. The main thread is eternally frozen at this point:

```(gdb) bt
#0  0x00007f635a89f042 in ?? () from /usr/lib/libc.so.6
#1  0x00007f635a8931ac in ?? () from /usr/lib/libc.so.6
#2  0x00007f635a8931f4 in ?? () from /usr/lib/libc.so.6
#3  0x00007f635a90d4ee in poll () from /usr/lib/libc.so.6
#4  0x00007f62f1612ba3 in ?? () from /usr/lib/libnvidia-glcore.so.580.95.05
#5  0x00007f62f1a3c559 in ?? () from /usr/lib/libnvidia-glcore.so.580.95.05
#6  0x00007f62f1a4e2aa in ?? () from /usr/lib/libnvidia-glcore.so.580.95.05
#7  0x00007f62f1956ade in ?? () from /usr/lib/libnvidia-glcore.so.580.95.05
#8  0x00005645ef725ce1 in RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::fence_wait (this=0x564624e8cc30, p_fence=...) at drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp:2621
#9  0x00005645f22d502c in RenderingDevice::_stall_for_frame (this=this@entry=0x564624c31e90, p_frame=0) at servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:6497
#10 0x00005645f22df857 in RenderingDevice::_begin_frame (this=0x564624c31e90, p_presented=true) at servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:6345
#11 0x00005645f244afa1 in RenderingServerDefault::_draw (this=0x56462491de20, p_swap_buffers=true, frame_step=<optimized out>) at servers/rendering/rendering_server_default.cpp:97
#12 0x00005645ed7b00d7 in Main::iteration () at main/main.cpp:4776
#13 0x00005645ed7068e6 in OS_LinuxBSD::run (this=this@entry=0x7ffd8fd6abc0) at platform/linuxbsd/os_linuxbsd.cpp:991
#14 0x00005645ed67aa47 in main (argc=<optimized out>, argv=0x7ffd8fd6b208) at platform/linuxbsd/godot_linuxbsd.cpp:85
```

`vkWaitForFences` [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a4607f45227d7179e8979d5bd8288461e8e00de9/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp#L2621C18-L2621C33) never returns and is stuck on a loop that keeps `poll()`ing a socket internally in the driver. Is this something that could be an issue on the Godot/Wayland front? It would seem really bizarre to me if it's a driver error and it reproduces on all Wayland compositors, doesn't reproduce on X11 and only happens with 3+ total windows.

Edit 2: Did some more digging with vkconfig. Validation layers report a bunch of:

```
Validation Warning: [ BestPractices-ConcurrentUsageOfExclusiveImage ] | MessageID = 0x9070e9b8
vkCmdDrawIndexed(): Subresource (arrayLayer: 0, mipLevel: 0) of image is used on queue family index 0 after being used on queue family index 1, but has VK_SHARING_MODE_EXCLUSIVE, and has not been acquired and released with a ownership transfer operation
Objects: 1
    [0] VkImage 0x410000000041
```

at the start and nothing else afterwards, which doesn't seem too useful. API dump reports, as expected, `vkGetFenceStatus` as the last call. I've uploaded both the validation layer output and the API dump layer output [here](https://gist.github.com/freenull/00fdf76c08f8bdc09ba22869fc284d89) along with the vkconfig settings I used. The output is from running Godot 4.5.1 right inside the project directory of the example linked in the OP (no editor inbetween). Note that the API dump uncompressed is over 105MiB.

I'm not a graphics programmer so I'm kind of just trying to throw everything I can find against this :/

FWIW, the [SDL Vulkan example](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/b31c4b70b3031dc4eb873612d65595a31b439a30/test/testvulkan.c) allows spawning multiple windows with `--windows 3` and it works perfectly fine, so it doesn't seem like the drivers or compositors are broken.

I should've known that with NVIDIA, the driver is always involved...
I've been running 580.95.05 so far for all of the previous tests. I installed a couple older versions of the NVIDIA drivers (incl. the Vulkan userspace). The issue **did not reproduce on 575.64.05**, on the exact same system otherwise. It reproduced on 580.95.05, the next released version according to NVIDIA's [archive page](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/unix/linux-amd64-display-archive/).

One look at the [release notes for that version](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/details/251355/) and there's this line:

> Added support for the fifo-v1 Wayland protocol on Vulkan.

Couldn't be more perfect - it's the exact combo of Linux, NVIDIA, Wayland and Vulkan. I went ahead and built a custom version of Godot with `WaylandThread:is_fifo_available` forced to return `false`. I also built a custom version of KWin where I completely ripped out fifo-v1 support (I basically manually reverted [this patch](https://invent.kde.org/plasma/kwin/-/merge_requests/6474)). Unfortunately, despite Godot correctly reporting that fifo-v1 is not available and there being literally no mention of fifo left in KWin, the issue is not fixed on versions after 575.64.05 :/

I also found out that Hyprland doesn't support fifo-v1 yet (and it reproduces too), so that should've been a hint too.

I figured out why there is a discrepancy between compositors where some take 7s and some 14s - it's entirely dependent on framerate! If I disable VSync, the program freezes almost instantly (unfortunately for some reason I can't get the program to run without VSync anymore even when disabled, maybe because I'm back on an unpatched KWin). I did some messy debugging where I launched Godot with GDB, broke on `frame_wait`:

```
break RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::fence_wait
```

then I `run` the program. Once it broke on the first fence_wait, I did:

```
python [gdb.execute('cont') for x in range(939)]
```

This spams the `cont` command 939 times, essentially rendering 940 frames (including the initial break). Then, **consistently** the 941st breakpoint trigger never comes. No matter how many times I redo this, it's always the 941st frame, as long as the monitor is set to 144Hz. If I set it to 60Hz, the number is slightly lower, but it's always ~940 frames. Those 940 frames divided by 144 FPS result in around 6.53s, while at 60 FPS the time until hang is around 15.67s - and this matches fairly well with the results under different compositors. So the time is unrelated, it happens after a set amount of frames. For some reason under some compositors the program is locked to 60FPS instead of 144, but that's not relevant.

So this now seems almost certainly a driver regression of some sort, but there's still a nagging question in my head about how SDL's testvulkan works (which to my Vulkan-noob eyes appears to be very similar in terms of semaphore/fence usage) yet Godot doesn't. I would really appreciate some feedback on these findings so that I can be a bit more certain this is actually a regression in the driver and report this on the NVIDIA forums.

Doesn't seem to be anything directly relevant in the [changelog](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/details/259267/):

> - Raised the minimum supported Wayland version to 1.20.
> - Fixed a bug that prevented the PowerMizer preferred mode dropdown menu in the nvidia-settings control panel from functioning correctly on Wayland.
> - Raised the minimum supported glibc version to 2.27.
> - Improved the performance of recreating Vulkan swapchains. This helps prevent stuttering when resizing Vulkan application windows.
> - Raised the minimum supported X.Org xserver version to 1.17 (video driver ABI version 19).
> - Fixed a bug that caused the Dots Per Inch (DPI) to be incorrectly reported for some monitors such as the Samsung Odyssey Neo G9.
> - Fixed several problems that prevented Vulkan applications from working on Venus VirtIO virtual GPU.
> - Fixed a bug that could cause system freezes on PREEMPT_RT kernels.

Possibly a side effect of one of the Wayland/Vulkan changes, or just not mentioned. I guess I will close this now, if it still reproduces for anyone ~~I will reopen~~ nevermind, no perms to reopen self-closed issues. If it still happens in any situation it's probably a different bug anyway.
